LESSON: KEEPING

Grade: Grade 2
Subject: ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIVITIES
Strand: Social
Topic 2.1.2: Keeping

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello learner! Today we will learn about Keeping. Read carefully, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. outline the importance of a clean school environment
2. participate in keeping the school environment clean
3. appreciate a clean school environment for health and safety. activities.

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

1. outline the importance of a clean school environment
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to outline the importance of a clean school environment. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

2. participate in keeping the school environment clean
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to participate in keeping the school environment clean. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

3. appreciate a clean school environment for health and safety. activities.
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to appreciate a clean school environment for health and safety. activities. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: At school, pick litter and put it in the bin. That cares for the environment.

Example 2: Wash your hands with soap before eating and after using the toilet.

Example 3: Name two foods you eat at home that help you grow strong.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Read the examples above again. Underline two new words or ideas about Keeping.
2. Explain Keeping to a parent or classmate using your own words and one Kenyan example.

4. Show that you can: outline the importance of a clean school environment
5. Complete the Work to do section, then attempt the Revision Quiz. Check Answers only after you finish.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Keeping. Use examples from your school, home, or market.
2. Answer this question in your exercise book: Why is Keeping important to you?
3. Make a short oral presentation (about one minute) to your parent or teacher.
